title: Tailwind profile: latency vs cost playbook (draft)
content:
Summary:

This note documents a focused set of microbenchmarks and a short playbook for dealing with an observed burst pattern we call a "tailwind profile": frequent, short (~50–200ms) surges that ride along a non-zero baseline and systematically shift mid-to-high percentiles (p75–p99) without large throughput changes.

Why this matters:
- Tailwind surges are common for conversational UIs that combine background telemetry/analytics calls with user-facing generation; the baseline load plus these tiny surges inflate p90/p95 while leaving average latency and throughput largely unchanged.
- Typical burst remedies (larger instance sizes, naive prewarm) are expensive and often miss the right trade-offs because they assume large, infrequent spikes rather than persistent short microspikes.

Goals for this pilot:
1) Quantify the p50/p90/p99 shifts caused by tailwind surges across common runtime knobs.
2) Produce a prioritized, low-friction mitigation playbook (knobs + config values) that reduces p95 by at least 20% while holding cost delta <= 10% in our synthetic scenarios.
3) Produce a short artifact (this doc) that teams can reuse as a checklist when they see similar profiles in Console.

Testbed and assumptions:
- Model: open-llm-13B-quant (INT8-ish profile used in internal experiments)
- Hardware: two node classes: Core-GPU (A100-80GB equivalent) and Edge-GPU (T4-like)
- Baseline session mix: 60% short-turn chat (10–20 tokens), 40% long-turn (200–600 tokens); tailwind surges are injected as ephemeral background requests (1–3 tokens) at 10–20% of user sessions, jittered.
- Batching: continuous batching enabled with slot pacing = ON by default
- KV cache: cold start every 6 min for sessions; tailwind surges often hit shared KV cache slots
- Cost metric: dollars per 100k generated tokens (approx amortized infra + energy estimate)

Measurement approach:
- For each configuration we capture: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 latency (client-observed end-to-end), throughput, and estimated cost per 100k tokens.
- Compare three knobs/controls: (A) slot pacing multiplier (0.5, 1.0, 2.0), (B) prefetch scope (none, session-only, global-prefix), (C) KV-hinting rate (off, low, aggressive).
- Run 30 minutes per condition, repeat 3 times; summary numbers below are median-of-runs.

Representative results (abridged):

Table: single-node Core-GPU, baseline QPS 120, with tailwind spikes ~15% of sessions

Condition | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | cost ($/100k tokens)
---------|---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------------------:
base (slot=1, no prefetch, kv=off) | 38 | 210 | 360 | 820 | 4.8
slot=0.5 (aggressive packing) | 44 | 260 | 470 | 1200 | 3.9
slot=2.0 (reserve slots) | 36 | 180 | 300 | 740 | 6.1
session-prefetch | 40 | 200 | 330 | 740 | 5.2
global-prefix-prefetch | 39 | 175 | 280 | 720 | 6.6
kv-hint=aggressive | 41 | 160 | 260 | 680 | 5.9

Key patterns to note:
- Aggressive packing (slot=0.5) reduces cost by ~19% but increases p95/p99 substantially — packing increases contention at small time scales that tailwind surges exacerbate.
- Reserving slots (slot=2.0) reduces p99 but increases cost substantially (~27% higher).
- Global prefix prefetch + kv-hinting gives the best p95 reduction (~23% vs base) at a moderate cost increase (10–25% depending on node class).
- On Edge-GPU node class the delta between prefetch and reserved slots is larger: prefetching dominates because the overhead of cold starts on smaller GPUs is higher.

ASCII illustration: p95 vs cost tradeoff (normalized)

Normalized cost (1.0 = base) -> [0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2,1.4]
Solutions (p95 normalized):
slot=0.5   : ||||========> (p95=1.30) cost=0.81
slot=1.0   : |||=========> (p95=1.00) cost=1.00
slot=2.0   : ||=========>  (p95=0.83) cost=1.27
global-pref: |=========> (p95=0.77) cost=1.25
kv-hint=aggr: |=======>   (p95=0.72) cost=1.23

Interpretation: packing trades cost for higher tail; prefetching and KV hinting buy tail improvements with similar cost delta to increasing reserved slots, but with less absolute cost growth on workloads with many short bursts.

Short playbook (priority ordered):
1) Detect tailwind pattern: add a console alert rule (p95/p99 rising while p50 and throughput stable; increased small (1–5 token) request fraction). Link: JIRA-OPT-889 for rule proto.
2) Enable session-scoped prefetch (quick toggle) for models with high short-turn ratios. Expected: ~15–25% p95 improvement, cost +8–12%.
3) If prefetch insufficient, enable KV-hinting aggressive for hot prefixes. Expected: additional 5–10% p95 improvement, cost +2–6%.
4) Avoid aggressive packing (slot multiplier < 0.7) for tailwind-prone tenants unless cost pressure cannot be relaxed — it amplifies tail risk.
5) As a fallback, scale-up to larger instance (reserve slots) only if p99 >= SLA threshold; accept cost delta.

Operational checklist (for SRE/product rollout):
- Instrumentation: capture small-request fraction metric (1–5 token calls / total), correlate with p95 uplift windows.
- Run the prefetch + kv-hint AB test for one week on 10–20% traffic. Collect p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics.
- If p95 improvement >= 15% and cost delta <= 12%: roll to 50% then 100% with monitoring.
- If p95 improves but cost delta > 20%: consider per-tenant policy (enable prefetch only for tenants whose SLA warrants it).

Open questions & next experiments:
- Interaction with persistent sessions & KV eviction policy (we used 6 min cold window here); outcome may vary if sessions are much longer.
- Memory-pressure effects on multi-tenant nodes when global-prefetch is enabled — need a 24h soak with simulated high tenancy.
- How quantization profiles (INT8 vs INT4) change prefetch effectiveness — the compute-to-memory ratio shifts.

Action items (owners):
- Samir: implement the tailwind detection rule prototype in Console (next 2 sprints).
- Priya: run multi-tenant 24h soak with global-prefetch on Edge nodes and report memory eviction patterns (run this week).
- Arielle: draft short customer-friendly one-pager summarizing the tailwind playbook and knob recommendations (deliver by next Monday).

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands (internal)
- quick-sample: query telemetry for session-mix: `SELECT pct_small_requests, p50, p95 FROM telemetry WHERE model='open-llm-13B-quant' AND window=5m`
- prefetch toggle: `redwoodctl runtime set-prefetch --model open-llm-13B-quant --scope session`

Notes: this is a draft. Numbers are synthetic and intended to illustrate trade-offs, not to be used as absolute guarantees. Feedback welcome, especially from Platform and SRE on multi-tenant leak/saturation scenarios.

-- end of draft --
